questions.text:
Consider the set of relations given below and the SQL query that follows:
 Students: (Roll_number, Name, Date_of_birth )

Coursed: (Course_number, Course_name, Instructor )

Grades: (Roll_number, Course_number, Grade)

SELECT DISTINCT Name

FROM Students, Courses, Grades

WHERE Students.Roll_number = Grades.Roll_number

                            AND   Courses.Intructor =Sriram

                            AND   Courses.Course_number = Grades.Course_number

                            AND   Grades.Grade = A
Which of the following sets is computed by the above query?
questions.solution:
The joins pair each student with a grade row and its course. The conditions keep rows where the course is taught by Sriram and the grade is A. DISTINCT then lists every student with at least one such row; nothing checks "all courses".

Answer: Names of Students who have got an A grade in at least one of the courses taught by Sriram

options: Names of Students who have got an A grade in all courses taught by Sriram
Names of Students who have got an A grade in all courses
Names of Students who have got an A grade in at least one of the courses taught by Sriram

questions.text:
For a database relation R(a,b,c,d) where the domain of a,b,c and d include only atomic value, only the following functions dependencies and those that can be inferred from them hold
a[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]c
b[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]d
The relation is in:
questions.solution:
The only key is {a, b}. a [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] c and b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] d are partial dependencies (part of the key determines a non-key attribute), so R is not in 2NF. Atomic values make it 1NF.

Answer: First normal form but not in second normal form

Second normal form but not in third normal form

questions.text:
Given relations R(w,x) and S(y,z), the result of
SELECT DISTINCT w,x
FROM R,S
is guaranteed to be same as R, if
questions.solution:
R [latex]\times[/latex] S repeats each R tuple |S| times; DISTINCT w, x removes the repeats. The result equals R only if S is non-empty (otherwise the product is empty) and R has no duplicates (DISTINCT would remove them).

Answer: R has no duplicates and S is non-empty

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: R has no duplicates and S is non-empty
R and S have no duplicates
S has no duplicates and R is non-empty
R and S have the same number of tuples

questions.text:
Considering the following table in a relational database :
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text { Last Name } & \text { Rank } & \text { Room } & \text { Shift } \\ \hline \text { Smith } & \text { Manager } & 234 & \text { Morning } \\ \hline \text { Jones } & \text { Custodian } & 33 & \text { Afternoon } \\ \hline \text { Smith } & \text { Custodian } & 33 & \text { Evening } \\ \hline \text { Doe } & \text { Clerical } & 222 & \text { Morning } \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
According to the data shown in the table, which of the following could be a candidate key of the table?
questions.solution:
A candidate key must be unique in every row:
- Last Name: "Smith" repeats False
- Room: 33 repeats False
- Shift: "Morning" repeats False
- {Room, Shift}: (234, Morning), (33, Afternoon), (33, Evening), (222, Morning) are all different True

Answer: {Room, Shift}

questions.text:
Consider the following four relational schemas. For each schema, all non-trivial functional dependencies are listed. The underlined attributes are the respective primary keys.

Which one of the relational schemas above is in 3NF but not in BCNF?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: a set-valued attribute violates 1NF.
- II: keys are (rollno, courseid) and (email, courseid). In email [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] rollno, email is not a superkey, but rollno is prime [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] allowed in 3NF, not in BCNF True
- III: marks [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] grade is transitive with a non-prime target [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not 3NF.
- IV: courseid [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] credit is a partial dependency [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not 2NF.

Answer: Schema II
